analysis: Examined the BASE excerpts of landing/package-lock.json (lines 1587-3093) plus the file_changes patch excerpt. The PR is a dependency bump for the marketing landing site (landing/package-lock.json). It raises next from 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 and sharp from 0.34.5 to 0.35.5. It also raises libvips from 1.2.4 to 1.3.4, raises the Node engine floor to >=20.9.0, and reshuffles the lockfile layout. The visible BASE region covers @typescript-eslint, eslint, jsdom and lightningcss, all dev-only transitive packages. Their changed ranges are mostly line shifts caused by the insertions earlier in the file. All resolved URLs in the visible text point to registry.npmjs.org and carry sha512 integrity hashes. I saw no git, http or tarball-URL sources, no registry redirection, and no install-script additions. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the head side of the changed ranges (for example head 1600-1663, and the new blocks near 626-645 and 1033-1061) was not visible and could not be fully checked. This package is a landing site and sits outside the provider and native-runtime scope of the threat model. It touches no assets (A-001 to A-018) and no trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, TB-012). The remaining question for integration is whether the head-side lockfile entries, such as the new sharp and libvips packages, keep registry.npmjs.org resolutions with integrity hashes. Nothing supplied suggests otherwise, so I raised no finding.
